title: introduce-kernel-queue-latency-matrix-and-token-drift-calibrator
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: we've seen recurring incidents where tail latency spikes correlate with kernel queueing on specific model variants during bursty traffic. Existing metrics surface GPU occupancy and batch sizes separately, but we lack a compact view that correlates kernel-queue depth, effective batch size, and per-token latency drift by model variant and route. This PR adds a new observability surface: a Kernel Queue Latency Matrix dashboard, per-variant matrix rollups, and an automated Token Drift Calibrator that tunes alert thresholds based on short-term percentile shifts.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds instrumentation and dashboards to surface kernel-queue-induced latency drift, implements a lightweight calibrator that computes delta-percentile for per-token latency per model-variant and adjusts alert bands as a suggestion (non-blocking), captures contextual log snapshots when drift crosses an adaptive threshold, and provides a small runtime hook to tag traces with queue-depth buckets to enable downstream correlation.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric producer: kernel_queue_depth gauge + kernel_queue_age histogram (sharded by model_variant, route)
- [x] Per-token latency histogram with variant/route labels and token_phase (decode/kvlookup)
- [x] Server-side trace enrichment: add trace.tag "kernel_queue_bucket" and "queue_age_ms" when queue depth > 0
- [x] Dashboard: Kernel Queue Latency Matrix (heatmap), Variant rollups, Drift scoring panel
- [x] Token Drift Calibrator service (read-only by default) that suggests alert threshold updates to SRE console
- [x] Lightweight log snapshotter that captures a bounded sample of request logs + prompt shape when drift triggers
- [x] Tests: unit tests for calibrator logic + integration test that validates metric labels emitted by a small simulated load generator
- [x] Docs: add short-runbook and dashboard docs under observability/docs

Commits (summary):
- commit a1b2c3d: add kernel_queue_metrics producer and expose via /metrics endpoint (instrumentation, prometheus exporter glue)
- commit d4e5f6a: add trace enrichment hook and queue bucket assignment in runtime scheduler
- commit 9f8e7d6: implement token_drift_calibrator microservice and CLI to preview suggested thresholds
- commit b1c2d3e: dashboard JSON + Grafana panels and example alerts (suggestions, not enforced)
- commit f6e5d4c: add log-snapshotter and sample extraction wiring + tests

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduling/kernel_queue_metrics.cc (new)
- runtime/scheduling/CMakeLists.txt (build)
- runtime/tracing/trace_enricher.go (mod)
- telemetry/calibrators/token_drift/main.py (new)
- telemetry/calibrators/README.md (new)
- observability/dashboards/kernel_queue_matrix.json (new)
- observability/alerts/token_drift_rules.yaml (new, suggestions only)
- tools/testbench/load_simulator.go (mod/add test harness)
- docs/observability/runbooks/kernel-queue-drift.md (new)
- ci/integration/token-drift-test.yaml (new)
- telemetry/log_snapshotter/snapshotter.rs (new)

Small illustrative snippets included inline in the dashboard JSON and calibrator (kept minimal):
- kernel_queue_bucket label values: [low, medium, high, saturated]
- calibrator algorithm: compute P50/P90 delta over 10-minute rolling window against 3h baseline; score = weighted(delta_p90, delta_p50) capped at 0-100; suggestions when score > 12

Review conversation (selected threads):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "Can we avoid making calibrator an automatic policy change? SRE should approve threshold moves."
  - Aisha: "Agree; calibrator is read-only and surfaces suggestions in SRE console. We added an opt-in flag for auto-apply but it's disabled by default."
- Marta Chen (comment): "Trace enrichment looks good; ensure we redact prompt tokens when capturing snapshots."
  - Aisha: "Added scrubber for prompt tokens and limits snapshot size to 8KB per invocation."
- Ravi Patel (request changes): "Make sure dashboard panels tolerate missing variant labels for older models. Also add unit tests for score calculation edge cases."
  - Aisha: "Added defensive aggregation and three extra unit tests covering NaN and empty-window behavior."
- SRE team (approval): "Approving for canary; recommend deploying calibrator read-only to staging for 48h before production."

CI checks and outcome (summary):
- unit-tests (linux): pass
- integration/token-drift (staging): intermittent fail on first run due to timing of simulated load; re-ran and pass
- lint (go/python/rust): pass with minor style suggestions applied
- security-scan: pass (no new external deps)
- perf-smoke: pass (PR-level microbench shows <1% median latency overhead)

Operational notes for rollout:
- Deploy order: 1) metric producer + trace enrichment to canary hosts, 2) enable dashboard read-only in Grafana, 3) run calibrator in read-only mode in staging for 48h, 4) review suggested threshold changes in SRE console, 5) optionally enable auto-apply behind feature flag after sign-off.
- Backout: metrics/traces are additive; removing dashboard and calibrator is non-disruptive. If auto-apply is enabled accidentally, revert via feature flag toggle in console.

Release notes (short):
- Added Kernel Queue Latency Matrix dashboard and per-variant drift scoring.
- Introduced Token Drift Calibrator service that recommends alert threshold adjustments based on short-term percentile shifts.
- Added trace enrichment to help correlate kernel queue depth with per-token latency.

Why this is different from prior work: instead of only emitting per-host GPU or token histograms, this PR focuses on the interaction between kernel queueing and token-phase latency at the model-variant level and provides a non-invasive, suggestion-first calibrator to reduce alert noise while surfacing real regressions.
